engagement_background.objective: APDerm engaged Treya Partners to reduce procurement costs, gain enterprise-wide spend visibility, and leverage its purchasing power across a fragmented, multi-location supply base in order to create EBITDA / enterprise value for its private-equity owner during an inflationary, supply-constrained market.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya executed a two-phase strategic sourcing program covering more than 10 indirect spend categories with a combined baseline of roughly $6.3 million. Phase 1 tackled high-value areas such as medical supplies, courier, telecom, IT hardware, office supplies and small-parcel; Phase 2 focused on eight additional categories—Billing Services, Janitorial, IT Managed Services, Laundry/Linen, Non-IT Temp Labor, Copier/Print Services, Uniforms, and (initially) Waste Management—representing about $3.5 million in annual AP spend. Waste Management was later removed from scope after a new Stericycle contract limited savings potential.
constraints_challenges: Decentralized purchasing across dozens of New England clinic locations that were added through acquisitions, resulting in a fragmented supplier landscape.
Minimal spend visibility and inconsistent AP data—significant vendor deduplication and GL mapping effort required to establish a usable baseline.
Limited internal procurement resources; client stakeholders needed to provide timely input while maintaining day-to-day clinic operations.
Ongoing pandemic-era inflation and supply-chain disruptions increased price volatility and supplier sensitivity.
Requirement to preserve clinical service quality and minimize operational disruption, favoring incumbent retention where possible.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable transaction data (10/1/20-9/30/21) was available in spreadsheets; contract files had to be manually collected from individual sites; no centralized contract repository or spend analytics system existed.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple vendor naming conventions, high percentage of 'Unmapped' spend, and gaps in supplier usage data necessitated vendor deduping and GL mapping before analysis; some suppliers never provided detail despite repeated requests.
